skill_title: Apply the ideal gas equation and kinetic theory of gases

items.question: Which equation is the ideal gas equation?
items.explanation: The ideal gas equation: pV = nRT (R is the universal gas constant).

items.question: In pV = nRT, what does n represent?
items.expectedAnswer: The number of moles of gas.
items.explanation: n is the amount of gas in moles.
options: The number of moles of gas.
The mass of the gas in grams.

items.question: In the ideal gas equation, temperature T must be in...
items.explanation: T must always be in kelvin in pV = nRT.

items.question: Which is an assumption of the kinetic theory of an ideal gas?
items.expectedAnswer: Gas particles have negligible volume and no forces between them.
items.explanation: Ideal gas particles are treated as point masses with no intermolecular forces, in constant motion.
options: Gas particles have negligible volume and no forces between them.
Gas particles attract each other strongly.

items.question: According to kinetic theory, the collisions between ideal gas particles are...
items.explanation: Ideal gas collisions are perfectly elastic — total kinetic energy is conserved.

items.question: Real gases behave MOST like ideal gases at...
items.explanation: At high T and low p, particles are far apart and fast, so forces and volume are negligible (most ideal).

items.question: What causes the pressure of a gas in a container?
items.expectedAnswer: Gas particles colliding with the container walls.
items.explanation: Pressure arises from the force of countless particle collisions with the walls.
options: Gas particles colliding with the container walls.

items.question: The average kinetic energy of gas particles depends on the gas's...
items.explanation: Average kinetic energy is proportional to the absolute (kelvin) temperature.

items.question: When using pV = nRT with SI units, pressure should be in...
items.explanation: In SI units pressure is in pascals, volume in m³, with R = 8.31 J·K⁻¹·mol⁻¹.

items.question: Heating a gas (at fixed volume) makes its particles move...
items.explanation: Higher temperature means greater average kinetic energy, so particles move faster.

items.question: How many moles of an ideal gas occupy 0.0249 m³ at 100 000 Pa and 300 K? (R = 8.31 J·K⁻¹·mol⁻¹)
A gas occupies 0.05 m³ at 200 000 Pa and 400 K. How many moles are present? (R = 8.31)
Why do real gases deviate from ideal behaviour at high pressure?
items.expectedAnswer: Particles are forced close together, so their volume and attractions are no longer negligible.
items.explanation: At high pressure the particles' own volume and intermolecular forces become significant, so real gases deviate.
options: Particles are forced close together, so their volume and attractions are no longer negligible.
The particles move faster than light.
Pressure has no effect on gases.

items.question: 2 moles of an ideal gas are at 300 K in a 0.05 m³ container. What is the pressure? (R = 8.31)
At the same temperature, which gas particles move faster on average: lighter or heavier ones?
items.expectedAnswer: Lighter particles (same average KE, smaller mass ⇒ higher speed).
items.explanation: At equal temperature the average KE is equal; lighter particles must move faster to have the same ½mv².
options: They move at the same speed.
Lighter particles (same average KE, smaller mass ⇒ higher speed).

items.question: What happens to gas pressure (fixed volume and amount) if the absolute temperature doubles?
items.explanation: From pV = nRT at fixed V and n, p ∝ T, so doubling T doubles p.

items.question: Why is the kinetic energy of gas particles said to be zero only at absolute zero (0 K)?
items.expectedAnswer: At 0 K particle motion theoretically stops, so kinetic energy is zero.
items.explanation: Absolute zero is the temperature at which particle motion (and kinetic energy) would theoretically cease.
options: At 0 K particle motion theoretically stops, so kinetic energy is zero.

items.question: A 0.5 mol sample of gas is at 250 000 Pa in 0.004 m³. What is its temperature? (R = 8.31)
Doubling the number of moles of gas (fixed T and V) does what to the pressure?
items.explanation: From pV = nRT at fixed T and V, p ∝ n, so doubling the moles doubles the pressure.

items.question: Which statement about an ideal gas is FALSE?
items.expectedAnswer: Its particles strongly attract each other.
items.explanation: Ideal gas particles are assumed to have NO intermolecular forces — the 'strong attraction' statement is false.
options: Its particles are in constant random motion.
Its particles strongly attract each other.
